title: observability-salience-mapper-and-alert-path-rewrite
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: reduce alert noise and accelerate SRE response by combining multi-signal salience scoring with deterministic alert routing. This PR introduces a Salience Mapper service and an Alert Path Rewriter that route alerts to teams and escalation policies based on signal composition (metrics, traces, logs, and token-cost deltas). The goal is to: 1) surface high-impact regressions faster, 2) lower false-positive paging for long-tail token-cost blips, and 3) provide richer context on the alert (top contributing tokens, model stage, kernel queueing snapshot) for runbook-driven triage.

What this change does (high level):
- New component: observability/salience-mapper (Go microservice) that consumes our observability event stream, computes a salience score using weighted heuristics (SLO delta, 95/99 latency shift, token-cost spike, trace error density, KV cache miss rate) and attaches a stable "salience_id" and top-3 contributing signals.
- Alert Path Rewriter: rules engine that rewrites alert routing metadata (team, escalation policy, preferred channel) based on salience buckets and model ownership tags extracted from the trace span.
- Dashboard: Grafana panel group under Observability -> Salience to visualize salience cohort heatmap, top contributing signals per cohort, and a compact time-series of salience-weighted incident rate.
- Telemetry: new OTEL attributes and Prometheus exporters for salience_score, salience_cohort, top_signal_tags and salience_id for cross-linking to traces and logs.
- Alert tuning: default alert dampening added for low-salience anomalies (auto-snooze window) and priority escalation rules for high-salience incidents.
- Tests and infra: unit tests for scoring heuristics, an integration harness (replaybench) to validate rewrites against synthetic incidents, updated Helm chart values to deploy the mapper in Dedicated and Private clusters.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc referenced (Linear ENG-4242) and reviewed by SRE/product.
- [x] Unit tests for mapper heuristics.
- [x] Integration replaybench validated route rewrites with representative traffic.
- [x] Grafana dashboards and alert runbooks added.
- [x] Helm values and k8s manifests updated for canary rollout.

Backward compatibility and safety: the Alert Path Rewriter only mutates non-critical routing labels by default and is gated behind a feature flag (observability.salience.enabled=false). We default to read-only mode (compute salience and attach attributes) for the first week of rollout; active routing changes require explicit enable.

Related: this complements ENG-4301 (alert-decay controller) and addresses a support ticket (SUP-1120) where nightly token-cost churn repeatedly paged on low-impact developer flows.

Notes: scoring heuristics are intentionally transparent (code comments + docs) so on-call can adjust weights without a code change. The mapper persists salience_id and a compact summary to our event-store (TTL 30d) to enable post-incident forensics and correlating long-tail regressions across releases.

release_notes: Add Salience Mapper to compute multi-signal salience scores and route alerts via Alert Path Rewriter. New Grafana Salience dashboard and alert dampening rules. Feature gated behind observability.salience.enabled. See docs/observability/salience-mapper.md for rollout steps.
notes_for_oncall: Key dashboards: Observability -> Salience -> Salience Cohort Heatmap. If an alert was rerouted unexpectedly, use /debug/rule-eval on the rewriter and inspect salience_id in trace attributes. To temporarily disable routing, set observability.salience.enabled=false in the Helm values and redeploy the rewriter replica set. Monitor salience_rewrite_rate and salience_snooze_count for unexpected behavior.
